title: Isolation of Nuclei from Adult Human Brain Tissue for 10x Genomics Platform
author: LeinU01 BRAIN grant
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.y6rfzd6
materials: 2 M Potassium Chloride, RNase free (KCl; Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9640G)
1 M Magnesium Chloride, RNase free (MgCl2; Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9530G)
1 M Tris Buffer, pH 8.0 (Ambion/Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9856)
Triton X-100 (Molecular biology grade, Sigma T8787)
Molecular Biology Grade Ethanol (Sigma E7023 or equivalent)
Millimark mouse anti-NeuN monoclonal antibody clone A60, PE conjugated (EMD Millipore FCMAB317PE)
PE mouse IgG1k isotype control (BD Biosciences, 555749)
Bottle-top vacuum filter system; 0.22 µm pore size, 250 ml (EMD Millipore, Millipore Steritop or equivalent) or 0.45 µm (Corning 430516 purchased as VWR 28199-814, 28199-818 or equivalent)
Syringe filter, 0.22 µm (EMD Millipore, Millex PES 30mm sterile syringe filters, SLGP033RB or equivalent)

steps.title: Gather reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all required reagents (frozen tissue 50‑500 mg, sucrose VWR 97061, 100 mM DTT Promega P1171, 10 % BSA, 10 % Triton‑X‑100, Nuclei Isolation Media components, 50X Protease Inhibitor Cocktail, DAPI, RNasin Plus, myelin removal beads Miltenyi 130‑096‑733, antibodies, etc.) and equipment (1.5 ml RNase‑free tubes Eppendorf 0030108051, 5 ml round‑bottom tubes BD Falcon 352235, 70 µm Miltenyi strainer 130‑098‑462, swinging‑bucket centrifuge with 1.7 ml/15 ml/50 ml rotors, 4 °C tube rotator Miltenyi MacsMini, house vacuum line with Tygon tubing Gast DOA‑P104‑AA, Dounce homogenizers Wheaton 357538 (1 ml) or 357542 (7 ml), 15 ml Dynamag magnet ThermoFisher 12301D, etc.) and place them in the biosafety‑level‑2 workspace.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % BSA solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 2 g ultrapure RNase‑free BSA into a 50 ml conical tube, add 20 ml nuclease‑free water, vortex until dissolved, let stand at room temperature 20 min to reduce foaming, filter through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a clean 50 ml tube, label, and store at 4 °C for up to 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % Triton‑X‑100 solution
steps.instruction: Measure 18 ml nuclease‑free water into a 50 ml conical tube, add 2 ml Triton‑X‑100, vortex until fully dissolved, let stand at room temperature 20 min, filter through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a clean 50 ml tube, label, and store at 4 °C for up to 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclei Isolation Media (NIM)
steps.instruction: In a RNase‑free 250 ml bottle add 200 ml nuclease‑free water, 2.5 ml 1 M Tris pH 8.0 (final 10 mM), 21.45 g sucrose (final 250 mM), 3.13 ml 2 M KCl (final 25 mM), 1.25 ml 1 M MgCl₂ (final 5 mM); cap and shake until sucrose dissolves, adjust volume to 250 ml with nuclease‑free water, filter using a 0.22 µm (Millipore Steritop) or 0.45 µm (Corning) filter attached via Tygon tubing to a 1000 ml filter flask connected to a house vacuum line, turn on vacuum, then store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Reconstitute 50X protease inhibitor cocktail
steps.instruction: Remove the cocktail from the –20 °C freezer, add 1 ml molecular‑biology‑grade 100 % ethanol with a P1000 pipette, pipette up/down 5‑10 times to dissolve, transfer to a PCR‑grade 1.5 ml RNase‑free tube, and store at 4 °C for up to 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg DAPI in 10 ml nuclease‑free water to make a 1 mg ml⁻¹ stock; aliquot 1 ml into labeled RNase‑free 1.5 ml tubes and freeze at –20 °C for up to 6 months. For use, thaw an aliquot and dilute 1:10 with nuclease‑free water to 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ (100 µg ml⁻¹); store the 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ solution at 4 °C for up to 1 month (the 1 mg ml⁻¹ stock can be kept at 4 °C for up to 3 months or returned to –20 °C).

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer (fresh)
steps.instruction: Measure 20 ml nuclease‑free water into a 50 ml conical tube, add 2.5 ml 10X PBS pH 7.4, add 2.5 ml BSA (final 1 %), vortex briefly, add 125 µl 40 U µl⁻¹ RNasin Plus (final 0.5 %, 0.2 U µl⁻¹), invert 5‑10 times to mix (do not vortex after RNasin), keep on ice or at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare homogenization buffer (fresh)
steps.instruction: Measure 24.125 ml NIM (pH 8.0) into a 50 ml tube, add 25 µl 100 mM DTT stock (final 0.1 mM), add 500 µl 50X protease inhibitor cocktail (final 1X), add 125 µl 40 U µl⁻¹ RNasin Plus (final 0.5 %, 0.2 U µl⁻¹), add 250 µl 10 % Triton‑X‑100 in nuclease‑free water (final 0.1 %), invert 5‑10 times to mix (do not vortex after RNasin), keep on ice or at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Decontaminate Dounce homogenizers
steps.instruction: Soak dounce bodies and pestles in RNase Away overnight, rinse thoroughly with MilliQ water then with nuclease‑free water, dry on a clean kimwipe, wrap each component in a clean kimwipe, place in a clean RNase‑free container (pipette tip box or Ziploc bag), and store at 4 °C for at least 30 min before use.

steps.title: Thaw and weigh tissue
steps.instruction: If using frozen tissue, remove from –80 °C, weigh 50‑150 mg (typical for 1 ml dounce). For 50‑100 mg add 1 ml homogenization buffer; for >100 mg add 7 ml buffer. Thaw on wet ice. If using microdissected sections, discard the original immersion buffer and add 1 ml homogenization buffer.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Place the appropriate dounce (1 ml for small pieces, 7 ml for larger) in an ice bucket with wet ice (prevent ice entry). Keep pestles wrapped until use. Transfer tissue and homogenization buffer to the dounce, insert the loose pestle and perform 10‑20 strokes while keeping the pestle submerged and the dounce on ice. Replace the loose pestle with the tight pestle and repeat 10‑20 strokes under the same conditions. Add an additional 5 ml homogenization buffer to the dounce.

steps.title: Filter homogenate and adjust volume
steps.instruction: Using a P1000 pipette, transfer the homogenate through a 70 µm cell strainer into a 15 ml conical tube, then through a 30 µm strainer into a second 15 ml tube; repeat the 30 µm filtration into a third 15 ml tube. Add homogenization buffer to bring the final volume to 10 ml per sample.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei
steps.instruction: Spin the filtered homogenate at 900 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes in a refrigerated centrifuge. A visible pellet should form at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the supernatant, leaving approximately 50 µl of liquid above the pellet; discard the removed supernatant into a waste container containing 10 % bleach.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3 ml blocking buffer to the pellet and gently pipette up/down until no tissue aggregates remain.

steps.title: Myelin removal bead incubation
steps.instruction: Add myelin removal beads (Miltenyi 130‑096‑733) at a 1:100 dilution (30 µl beads per 3 ml suspension), mix by pipetting up/down with a P1000 at least five times, and incubate on ice (4 °C) for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second blocking buffer addition
steps.instruction: Add another 3 ml blocking buffer, mix by pipetting up/down with a P1000 five or more times until the suspension appears homogeneous.

steps.title: Centrifuge post‑bead incubation
steps.instruction: Spin at 300 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes. Discard the supernatant, add 3 ml clean blocking buffer to the pellet, and resuspend gently by pipetting up/down with a P1000.

steps.title: Magnetic separation of myelin debris
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a 15 ml Dynamag magnet (ThermoFisher 12301D) positioned in a 4 °C refrigerator and incubate for 15 minutes. Then carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the magnetic pellet of myelin‑bead complexes and transfer it to a new 15 ml conical tube for downstream NeuN staining.

steps.title: Optional nuclei viability count
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µl nuclei suspension with 10 µl 0.4 % Trypan Blue, pipette up/down 5 times, incubate 1 minute at room temperature, load 10 µl into a disposable hemocytometer, examine under an inverted phase‑contrast microscope, and record nuclei integrity and, if desired, yield.

steps.title: Prepare control tubes
steps.instruction: Create two controls per experiment: (a) DAPI‑only control – set aside 50 µl nuclei suspension on ice; (b) Isotype control – add 450 µl blocking buffer to 50 µl nuclei suspension (final 500 µl). To the isotype tube add PE‑conjugated IgG1,k isotype antibody at 1:250 (2 µl per 500 µl). For each experimental sample (500 µl total), add mouse anti‑NeuN PE‑conjugated antibody at 1:500 (1 µl per 500 µl). Record which sample corresponds to each control.

steps.title: Incubate antibody labeling
steps.instruction: Incubate all tubes (samples and controls) on ice for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Post‑staining centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin all tubes in a refrigerated centrifuge at 400 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes using a swinging‑bucket rotor. Remove supernatant leaving ~50 µl above the pellet, add 2 ml clean blocking buffer, and resuspend by pipetting up/down five times. Adjust final volume if needed for FACS sorting.

steps.title: Add DAPI for sorting
steps.instruction: Add DAPI to a final concentration of 0.1 µg ml⁻¹ (dilute from the 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ stock) and mix gently by tapping each tube.

steps.title: Filter before FACS
steps.instruction: Transfer each sample into the cap of a 5 ml Polystyrene round‑bottom FACS tube and filter the suspension through the cap.

steps.title: Keep samples cold and proceed to FACS
steps.instruction: Maintain tubes on ice or at 4 °C until loading onto the flow cytometer.

steps.title: Dispose waste and clean equipment
steps.instruction: Dispose any unused blocking or homogenization buffer down the sink. Discard all tissue, contaminated liquids, and consumables in a biohazard waste container. Clean Dounce homogenizers by soaking in 10 % bleach for at least 20 minutes, rinse with tap water, soak overnight in RNase Away, rinse with MilliQ then nuclease‑free water, dry with clean kimwipes, wrap, and store in a clean RNase‑free container at room temperature until next use.
